newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - LUKoil looks at Russian selloff.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - LUKoil looks at Russian selloff.

text.p: Russia's largest oil company AO LUKoil will submit a bid in the privatisation of Norsi Oil, which is being sold by the government, LUKoil chairman Vagit Alekperov told Reuters in an interview.

Norsi operates one of Russia's largest refineries, processing 250,000 barrels of crude oil per day, and LUKoil already has a stake in the company, and LUKoil plans to provide 200,000 barrels of crude to Norsi.
"We have submitted a bid to the State Property Committee," Alekperov said.
Alekperov also said LUKoil may look at acquiring a stake in Rosneft, a vertically intgrated oil company which has large-scale operations in the Russian Far East.

Alekperov said LUKoil, which has a venture with Algerian state energy company Sonatrach, would also like to look at upstream deals outside the Former Soviet Union, but was constrained by lack of capital.
He said LUKoil was currently assessing four projects in Algeria, two crude oil projects, one exploration project and one natural gas project.
"If we went into an area like the North Sea, we would like to go in as a strategic partner as we have done in all of our deals in the former Soviet Union," Alekperov said.

He said that LUKoil, which on Friday announced that it would form a joint venture to retail petroleum in the U.S. with Nexus Fuels, would aim to start shipping crude oil from its oilfields via the Black Sea for refining in the U.S.
"We shall start approaching our partners, such as ARCO, Chevron Corp and Mobil Corp to ask them to refine our crude oil," Alekperov said.
He added that the company already had refining assets through the former Soviet Union and was looking at expanding in Eastern Europe.
"One market we are considering is Slovenia, which has very good refineries which can be used to process our crude oil," he said.

LUKoil's own refineries processed 348,000 barrels per day in the first three months of this year, it also claims the largest oil reserves of any private company in the world with 65.3 million tonnes at the end of 1996.
LUKoil is one of the mostly widely held Russian securities outside the country, by fixed income investors through its bond issues and its American Depositary Receipts, which are listed in London.

The company is one of the few with U.S. GAAP and international accounts and has a reserve audit conducted by Miller & Lents, essential in an era when Soviet reserve estimates are viewed with suspicion by foreign investors. ((David Chance, New York Newsroom 212 859 1902))
